[IALC.1.2] A build-time selector `DS_ALLOC_MODE` chooses how the macros
resolve. Its values are `DS_ALLOC_MACRO` (1) and `DS_ALLOC_WEAK` (2); it
must default to `DS_ALLOC_WEAK`, so every build is link-time-overridable
without a recompile. `DS_ALLOC_MACRO` is the explicit opt-out for a
byte-identical, zero-indirection build. When `DS_ALLOC_MODE` is unset but
`DS_ALLOC_HEADER` is defined, the mode is `DS_ALLOC_MACRO` — a named header is
an explicit request for inline expansion, so the weak default must never
silently ignore it.

- In `DS_ALLOC_WEAK` mode (the default) each macro expands to a call to the
  correspondingly-named weak function `ds_malloc`/`ds_calloc`/… declared
  in `ds_alloc.h` and defined in `ds_alloc.c` ([IALC.5]). The wrapper is a
  single tail-callable cold-path frame, never on the allocation-free
  `realtime`/`constspace` hot path ([IALC.8.2]).
- In `DS_ALLOC_MACRO` mode the macros expand **inline**: to the
  integrator's functions when a header named by `DS_ALLOC_HEADER` is
  included and defines them, otherwise to the libc functions of the same
  name. With no `DS_ALLOC_HEADER` this must be byte-identical to a direct
  libc call — the macro is transparent.
